messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Synthetic check 'canary-prober-eu-west' has crossed failure threshold in eu-west-1 (failure rate 48% over 5m). PagerDuty PD-78912 fired and notified on-call.

pagerduty-bot: PD-78912 — Triggered: canary-prober-eu-west. Paging @sre-alice (primary), escalation policy: 5m -> oncall-carol.

sre-alice: acked. I'll take ownership, jumping into triage now.

platform-ben: thanks — quick heads up, we just rolled a routing tweak for canary traffic to the new lb pool ~10m before this. could be related.

ops-dave: seeing the same in grafana: synthetic success rate dip and an increase in 5xx from the prober -> model-gateway. short window but repeating.

sre-alice: pulling prober logs now.

sre-alice: log tail from canary-prober-eu-west (last 2m):
```
2026-03-15T12:35:01Z ERROR probe failed status=503 target=/v1/generate host=model-gw-eu-1
2026-03-15T12:35:03Z WARN retrying attempt=1
2026-03-15T12:35:07Z ERROR probe failed status=503 target=/v1/generate host=model-gw-eu-1
2026-03-15T12:35:09Z INFO upstream-reset reason=503-throttle
```

platform-ben: can you curl the model-gateway from an exec inside the prober namespace? I want to confirm it's not a DNS or SG problem.

sre-alice: running quick check:
```
# kubectl -n synth exec -it deploy/canary-prober-eu-west -- curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://model-gw-eu-1.internal/v1/health
503
```

platform-ben: 503 from the gateway. opening the gateway logs.

deploy-bot: Deploy event: routing-config-v2 applied to lb-pool-eu at 2026-03-15T12:25:30Z by platform-ben.

oncall-carol: PD escalated to me (auto) — @sre-alice do you need backup?

sre-alice: thanks @oncall-carol — I'm seeing persistent 503s from model-gateway specifically on the lb-pool-eu nodes that we moved traffic to. will attempt to isolate by shifting prober to old pool and see if probes pass.

sre-alice: muting the PagerDuty rule for canary-prober-eu-west for 10m while we test to avoid noise.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-78912 has been silenced for 10 minutes (muted by sre-alice).

ops-dave: manually rerouting canary prober to lb-pool-eu-old:
```
kubectl -n synth set env deploy/canary-prober-eu-west CANARY_LB=lb-pool-eu-old
# redeploy to pick up env
kubectl -n synth rollout restart deploy/canary-prober-eu-west
```

sre-alice: restarted prober pods. waiting for new checks.

(2m later)

sre-alice: new probes now showing success 100% from rerouted pool. curl from a prober pod to model-gateway via old pool:
```
# kubectl -n synth exec -it deploy/canary-prober-eu-west -- curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://model-gw-eu-1.internal/v1/health
200
```

platform-ben: confirms — gateway returns 200 via lb-pool-eu-old but 503 through lb-pool-eu. looks like routing-config-v2 has an incompatible backend weight or health check mismatch.

oncall-carol: good catch. can we roll back the routing change or fix health-check config? We should treat as potential customer-impacting if the new pool had also been receiving production traffic.

sre-alice: I'm going to roll the routing change back (read-only rollout) and coordinate with platform to investigate root cause.

deploy-bot: Reverting routing-config-v2 on lb-pool-eu (triggered by sre-alice).

platform-ben: rolling back now and opening ENG-1234 to investigate health-check TTL and backend weights.

pagerduty-bot: PD-78912 auto-resolved (no active alerts) — incident marked resolved by silence and probe stabilization.

sre-alice: summary:
- Timeline: routing-config-v2 deployed ~12:25Z -> canary failures by 12:35Z -> prober reroute and silence at 12:38Z -> rollback at 12:42Z -> probes stable by 12:44Z.
- Impact: synthetic canaries in eu-west showed transient 5xxs; no sustained customer-facing 5xx spike in production API metrics (SLOs unaffected), but model-gateway node pool had unhealthy backends which would have affected any traffic hitting the new pool.
- Mitigation: reverted routing change, rerouted prober to old pool, muted PD noise, created ticket ENG-1234 for postmortem and hardening (health-check alignment + pre-deploy canary gating).

oncall-carol: thanks @sre-alice and team. please add the health-check snippet and reproduction steps to ENG-1234.

ops-dave: adding notes to the incident: affected region eu-west-1, prober name canary-prober-eu-west, PD id PD-78912.

sre-alice: closing loop — will follow up in postmortem doc and link to this thread. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: This thread has been marked as resolved for PD-78912. If further alerts appear, PD will re-open.
